contentHtml:
USA—The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Cogent Biosciences’ Ekitna (bezuclastinib) in combination with sunitinib for adults with advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumours (GIST) whose disease progressed or who could not tolerate previous imatinib treatment.

The approval, announced in November 2026, was supported by results from the global, randomised Phase III PEAK trial (NCT05208047), which compared the combination against sunitinib alone in patients with imatinib-resistant or intolerant GIST.

Phase III results support combination therapy

Data from the trial, collected up to September 30, 2025, showed that Ekitna combined with sunitinib reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 50% compared with sunitinib monotherapy, corresponding to a hazard ratio of 0.50.

An independent review also found that patients receiving the combination achieved a median progression-free survival (PFS) of 16.5 months, compared with 9.2 months among those receiving sunitinib alone.

The objective response rate was 46% in the combination group, against 26% in the comparator group, indicating a higher proportion of patients experienced tumour shrinkage with the two-drug regimen.

Cogent Biosciences President and CEO Andrew Robbins described the approval as an important milestone for the company and people living with GIST.

He said the PEAK trial results had supported the company’s confidence in the treatment and welcomed its availability as an additional option for patients requiring further therapy.

Commercial launch and patient support

Following the FDA decision, Cogent launched Ekitna alongside its Cogent Connect Patient Support Program.

The initiative is designed to help patients and healthcare professionals navigate treatment access and related support services.

Bezuclastinib is a selective tyrosine kinase inhibitor designed to target KIT mutations, including alterations affecting exon 17.

KIT mutations play a central role in the development and progression of GIST, making the protein an important target for precision cancer therapies.

The combination with sunitinib also expands treatment options for patients whose disease no longer responds adequately to imatinib, the established initial treatment for advanced GIST.

Beyond Ekitna, Cogent Biosciences is advancing a pipeline of targeted therapies directed at several cancer-related pathways, including erythroblastic oncogene B2 (ErbB2), Janus kinase 2 (JAK2), KRAS, and phosphoinositide 3-kinase alpha (PI3Kα).

The approval adds another targeted treatment to the advanced GIST market, where drug developers are pursuing therapies that address resistance to existing kinase inhibitors.

For Cogent, the commercial launch also creates an opportunity to establish its presence in the precision oncology market while advancing its broader clinical pipeline.
